text:
mike: Heads up — noticed a regression on the dashboard micro-sparklines after the routing-policy tweak last night. Interactions (filter toggles / time window) cause 400–900ms main-thread blocks and janky scrubbing.
anya: ugh. can you share a flame or HAR? is it the chart library or our data prep?
mike: quick flame shows long tasks inside render loop. Mostly in `aggregateAndNormalize()` and then DOM style recalcs. Also a few obvious `chart-utils` dynamic imports firing on first interaction.
evan: I saw a pattern like this earlier when request fan-out to the agg service increased latency. Could the routing change be sending small, fragmented requests to a slow backend?
mike: Possibly. Frontend makes per-widget aggregation requests when filters change. If those backend requests hit a cold or low-quota pool we get higher response tail and that forces sync updates.
lina: @mike can you repro with local throttling? Also paste the small code snippet where you call the aggregator.
mike: yeah here's the call:
```
// called on every filter change
const res = await fetch(`/api/v1/agg?series=${id}&from=${from}&to=${to}`);
const points = await res.json();
setPoints(points.map(p => normalize(p)));
```
We also do `import('chart-utils').then(run)` in the component mount.
jordan: two quick ideas: 1) debounce filter->fetch by 120ms so multiple quick toggles collapse, 2) move per-point normalize off main thread (worker) or push aggregation server-side.
anya: also check telemetry. If we emit high-cardinality events per datapoint on every render, that could flood the metrics pipeline and add latency in our sync hooks (we still await some telemetry flush in dev-mode).
perf-bot: perf alert (1950001200): sudden increase in long tasks on dashboard page x3 since 1950000300. Top stack frames: aggregateAndNormalize, applyStyles, dynamicImport(chart-utils).
deploy-bot: deploy 2024-11-06T03:12:40Z completed: routing-policy-v2 -> canary on 10% of traffic.
mike: that matches, regression started after canary widened.
evan: platform note — routing-policy-v2 introduced route-level quotas that split traffic by hash, but small customers end up on a backup pool with limited throughput. We'll investigate fallback pool throttling.
lina: short-term frontend mitigations: debounce + show low-res placeholder while fetching, prefetch chart-utils earlier (on hover) not mount. Also memoize normalize: `useMemo(() => points.map(...), [points])`.
jordan: platform medium-term: increase burst capacity for the fallback pool, and change routing to prefer busy pools with available capacity instead of strictly hashing. Also add a telemetry sample rate for datapoint-level events.
mike: I'm going to push a quick debounce + prefetch patch to canary and disable datapoint telemetry in dev. Will report back.
anya: thanks — if you need a hotfix, tag me. Also open a tiny runbook entry so support can triage user reports (chart jank -> routing canary rollback).
mike: filed quick PR and canary diff: `sparklines-debounce-prefetch`. will hold for 30m and monitor traces. :eyes:
